evidence.fact: Mount Olympus Traverse: 45 miles with 8,100 ft gain - West, Middle and East peaks, whole outing; Blue Glacier West Peak 44 mi RT, 7,400 ft.

note: 8,100 is a whole multi-peak traverse figure (excluded by rule 3), not a one-way gain; no published one-way traverse gain found. Neither value supported.

evidence.fact: Emmons Glacier from White River Campground: Elevation Gain 10,000 ft; profile TH-camp 5,100 + camp-summit 4,900.
Emmons-Winthrop: ~11 miles from White River to the summit, Elevation Gain: 10,000 feet.

note: Two independent publishers give exactly 10,000 from White River. Stored 10,300 is only 3% off (also within 10%), so this is a minor correction.

evidence.fact: Intro text: 'scramble of 13 miles and 3,500 feet of elevation gain'; the stats box on the same page says 4,000 ft.
Mount Stickney via Olney Creek road / One Acre Lake: Distance 6 miles, Elevation Gain 3,500 feet.

note: The Mountaineers page contradicts itself (3,500 in prose, 4,000 in stats; 12.5% apart, so they disagree); the independent WillhiteWeb page from the same Olney Creek road start gives 3,500.

evidence.fact: Trailhead past second Big Creek crossing (3,100 ft); stats: 8.0 mi, Elevation Gain 5,255 ft, High Point 6,255 ft.
Approach about 1 mile, 2,000 ft gain to the base; descent by the standard route 1.4 miles, 3,200 ft.

note: No second page gives a trailhead-to-summit gain. The Mountaineers' own trailhead (3,100) and high point (6,255) fit only about 3,155 ft one-way, so 5,255 looks wrong, but that is arithmetic and not a source. MP route page has no gain; Mazamas copies the Mountaineers text.

evidence.fact: Stats only: Elevation Gain 7,300 ft, High Point 7,756 ft; no trailhead or approach stated.

note: No second page found for this route. Stored 7,100 is within 10% of 7,300 (2.7%), so the two do not really disagree; no change needed either way.

evidence.fact: Stats only: Elevation Gain 7,300 ft, High Point 7,756 ft; no trailhead or approach stated.

note: No second page found. Stored 7,100 is within 10% of 7,300 (2.7%); not a real dispute.

evidence.fact: North Face from end of White Salmon Road: Elevation Gain 6,100 ft; profile trailhead-camp 2,500, camp-summit 3,600.
Mt. Shuksan, North Face; trailhead Mt. Baker Ski Area / White Salmon Lodge; Elevation Gain 6,100.

note: Weak: Mazamas also gives 6,100 for the Sulphide Glacier (a different trailhead), so its figure may be peak-generic. Stored 5,500 is 9.8% below 6,100, so it also agrees within 10%; the change is small.

evidence.fact: Sulphide Glacier from the Shannon Ridge (FR 1152-014) trailhead: 16.0 mi, Elevation Gain 6,500 ft.
Sulphide Glacier from Shannon Ridge Trailhead: 13.62 miles out-and-back, Elevation Gain 6,230 ft.

note: All figures agree within 10% (stored 6,600 too; Mazamas 6,100). Kept the most route-precise page (Mountaineers, 6,500). Effectively no dispute.

evidence.fact: From Paradise (5,420 ft): prose says 'Climb 9,000 feet'; stats box says Elevation Gain 8,790 ft.
Disappointment Cleaver: ~9 miles from Paradise to the summit, Elevation Gain: 9,000 feet.

note: All three figures agree within 10%; stored 9,000 matches RMI and the Mountaineers prose exactly.

evidence.fact: From Paradise: stats Elevation Gain 10,000 ft, but trip profile lists trailhead-camp 4,100 and camp-summit 4,900.
Fuhrer Finger from Paradise: ~9000' Elevation Gain, 11 Miles RT, 2 Days.

note: 10,000 vs 9,010 is 9.9%, so technically within 10%; the trip report (~9,000) and the Mountaineers' own profile segments back the stored figure. Trip report gain is approximate. final_value 9,000 is the trip report's figure (a page value); stored 9,010 is effectively the same.

evidence.fact: Mount Rainier/Gibraltar Ledges from Paradise: Elevation Gain 9,010 ft (verifier's page).
Mt. Rainier, Gibralter Ledge, starting at the Paradise visitor center: Elevation Gain 9,000.

note: Not a real dispute (0.1% apart). Mazamas states exactly the stored 9,000.

evidence.fact: Mount Stone from Hamma Hamma Road via Putvin Trail / Lake of the Angels: 10.0 mi, Elevation Gain 5,012 ft.
Mount Stone from the Putvin Trail via Lake of the Angels: 7.5 mi out-and-back, 4,819 ft elevation gain.

note: Not a real dispute (stored 5,000 vs 5,012). Kept the Mountaineers' route-specific 5,012; 5,000 would be just as defensible. The Mountaineers page is titled South Couloir but describes the Putvin / St. Peter's Gate approach.

evidence.fact: Ruth and Icy traverse from Hannegan Campground: 16.0 mi, Elevation Gain 6,500 ft headline; profile TH-camp 3,600, camp-Icy summit 1,270 gain / 800 loss.
Ruth Mtn and Icy Peak trip report: Elevation gain 7,100 ft; distance 16 miles; car-to-car 13 hrs (whole two-peak outing).

note: Every figure found covers the whole two-peak outing (excluded by rule 3); no page gives a one-way trailhead-to-Icy-summit gain. Stored 8,000 is not supported either.

evidence.fact: Cascade Pass trailhead via Sahale Arm, over Sahale to Boston Glacier: Elevation Gain 5,400 ft; profile 3,900 + 200 (net) + 1,300.

note: No second page with a trailhead-to-summit gain (Hebert trip report and others give no total). The route goes over the Sahale/Boston col and drops to the glacier, so the 'net' camp-to-climb segment means 5,400 may undercount real one-way gain. Neither value confirmed.

evidence.fact: From the Blue Lake Trailhead (5,200 ft): 5.0 mi, Elevation Gain 2,372 ft, High Point 7,753 ft.
Approach to North Early Winter Spire from the Blue Lake Trail: 2.5 mi, 1,913 ft ascent - to the base of the climb only, not the summit.

note: No second trailhead-to-summit figure; the MP figure stops at the base. Stored 2,600 and found 2,372 are 8.8% apart, so they agree within 10%; no change needed.

evidence.fact: Preacher Mountain from the Middle Fork Trailhead via Rainy Lake: 11.0 miles round trip, 5,000 ft of elevation gain.
Preacher Mountain from the Middle Fork trailhead via Rainy Lake: Distance 6 miles, Elevation Gain 5,200 feet.

note: The two pages agree within 10% (3.8%). WillhiteWeb states 5,200 against a one-way distance, so I kept the stored 5,200; the Mountaineers 5,000 sits beside a round-trip distance.
